def: NIST's voluntary framework, released in January 2023, that organises AI risk work into the functions Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.
NIST AI 600-1, a companion to the AI RMF that names twelve risks specific to generative AI and suggests actions for each.
The policies, roles, processes and records by which an organisation governs its AI activity, as specified and audited under ISO/IEC 42001.
A document listing which management-system controls apply to an organisation and why any others are excluded.
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which sets obligations for AI systems and general-purpose models according to role and risk tier.

Under the EU AI Act, a system in a product-safety area or a listed use such as employment or credit, which must meet requirements on risk management, data, documentation, logging, oversight and robustness.
The EU AI Act roles of the party that develops and places an AI system on the market and the party that uses it professionally under its own authority.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, which postponed the high-risk obligations of the AI Act to December 2027 and August 2028.
Design measures that let people understand an AI system's outputs, notice over-reliance, override results and stop the system.
A register linking each risk to a control, a metric with a threshold, an owner and the date of the latest result, generated from evals and traces.
A broadly capable model, such as a large language model, whose developers have separate documentation and risk duties under the EU AI Act.
